Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

npnormalize 0.1.4

A new address column asked for in #9, and a defect the measurement for it turned up. Both were measured against the 3,687,435-row unified BMF; the scan is dev/scan-box-component.R, kept as the record, the way scan-unit-designators.R is for the designator list.

  • street_has_box, a second question about a box: does the street carry a box component, whether or not the whole street is one. is_po_box cannot answer it and should not be widened to — it is the gate that blanks the address key in np_addr_key(), so widening it would stop counting records at streets that are genuine buildings. Filers write the street on line 1 ending in the box word and carry the box number alone on line 2, and a consumer holding that bare number had nothing to tell a box number from a door:

    raw street street_key is_po_box street_has_box
    211 EMMET STREET SOUTH PO BOX 211 EMMET ST S PO BOX FALSE TRUE
    300 KENAN CENTER DRIVE - CAMPUS BOX 300 KENAN CENTER DR CAMPUS BOX FALSE TRUE
    ONE HARRISON PLAZA BOX 5079 ONE HARRISON PLAZA BOX 5079 FALSE TRUE
    PO BOX A PO BOX A FALSE TRUE
    PO BOX 1367 PO BOX 1367 TRUE TRUE
    22009 BOX ELDER RD 22009 BOX ELDER RD FALSE FALSE

    is_po_box implies street_has_box on every row, because the flag is read from the key np_normalize() publishes — so a consumer holding a cached street_key can recompute it without re-normalizing.

    The box word has to end the key, with at most digits or a single letter after it. That anchor is the whole guard, and the reason the pattern is not the unanchored BOX pfmatch keeps locally: a bare \bBOX\b matches 2,099 rows the anchored form does not, and 127 of them are streets named for a box (BOX SPGS RD, BOX ELDER ST, BOX RD). The anchored form flags 1 of those 405 rows, and that one is a box. BOXWOOD and BOXER never match either way.

    The flag adds 11,982 rows (0.325%) to the 579,602 is_po_box already reports: 562 a street then a bare BOX, 10,345 a street then BOX <number>, and 1,075 a lettered box (PO BOX A … PO BOX Z, which .np_pobox_pat misses because it requires digits). DRAWER and BIN were measured and left out at 55 and 28 rows, against a false positive already visible at that volume (1206 GRAIN BIN RD).

    street_unit is deliberately not changed by this. The flag says the street has a box, not that a companion number is that box’s — the street can name a suite as well (4347 W NORTHWEST HWY STE 130 BOX), and that call belongs to whoever holds the second line. 0.1.2 already removed the sharp edge by making np_unit_id("400891") NA; this adds the positive signal a consumer can key on, and lets pfmatch replace its local .PF_BOX_RE with a column.

  • .np_parse_street() now treats only an anchored box as a box. Its gate was an unanchored grepl("\\bBOX\\b"), which overwrote the parse of 14,014 BMF rows (0.380%) whose street merely carries or is named for a box, on rows where is_po_box said FALSE:

    street_key 0.1.3 street_num / street_name 0.1.4
    ONE HARRISON PLZ BOX 5079 5079 / PO BOX NA / ONE HARRISON PLZ BOX 5079
    22009 BOX ELDER RD NA / PO BOX 22009 / BOX ELDER (type RD)
    211 EMMET ST S PO BOX NA / PO BOX 211 / EMMET ST S PO BOX
    PO BOX 12 12 / PO BOX 12 / PO BOX

    A BOX-named street used to lose its house number to a box number it does not have, and two records agreed on a street_num neither had. The parse and is_po_box can no longer disagree about what a box is, which a test asserts.

  • This moves the signature, to v1-1179714ce1e9d31f. street_has_box is a new cached column and street_num / street_name move on the rows above, so matchdb must rebuild its derived columns again — the 0.1.3 rebuild (matchdb#29) had already closed, so this does not ride along with it.

  • npmatch needs no change: it reads is_po_box only for geo_pobox, and the new column is additive.

npnormalize 0.1.3

Two parsing rules that 0.1.2 carried further, found when matchdb rebuilt under it (matchdb#29). Neither changes street_key, so blocking is unaffected.

  • A line naming several units keeps the most specific one, not the first one written. Every unit is cut from street_key, but street_unit holds one, and the first was often the one that does not tell occupants apart:

    raw street 0.1.2 street_unit 0.1.3
    1 BETHANY RD BUILDING 1 STE 5 BLDG 1 STE 5
    2125 BISCAYNE BLVD STE 204 # 22915 STE 204 # 22915
    1633 MAIN ST STE A PMB 175 STE A PMB 175
    123 MAIN ST RM 3 FL 2 RM 3 RM 3

    The rank (.np_unit_rank) runs building < floor or area < door < mailbox, and between two of one rank the last wins, because an address is written from the outside in. In matchdb’s 13.0M address strings, 56,466 name two or more units, and the pick changes for 54,936 of them (17,724 current address rows), mostly a mail store’s suite giving way to the customer’s box. The second address line is read by the same rule.

  • The house number is a whole leading token. An ordinal street has none: 16TH ST gave street_num 16T and street_name H, so two such records agreed on a house number neither has. Grid numbers stay whole (16W540 BLUFF RD, which gave 16W), and a number run into the street name is its digits (921AIRPORT SERVICE RD gives 921 on AIRPORT SERVICE, not 921A on IRPORT SERVICE) unless they could begin an ordinal. 19,909 of matchdb’s address strings change.

  • This moves the signature, to v1-592912060053c4c3. Cached street_unit, street_unit_id, street_num and street_name values must be rebuilt.

npnormalize 0.1.2

Two unit-extraction bugs reported from pfmatch, which parses the free-text secondary-unit line of Form 990-PF Part XIV Table 3a with this package (#7).

  • BUILDING is now a unit designator, as its abbreviation BLDG already was. The unit is extracted from the raw street, while .np_street_types contracts BUILDING -> BLDG two lines later in np_normalize(), so the pattern never saw the one spelling it recognized and the two spellings of one address disagreed on both outputs:

    raw street street_key street_unit
    100 CAMPUS CENTER BUILDING 86E was 100 CAMPUS CENTER BLDG 86E was NA
    100 CAMPUS CENTER BLDG 86E 100 CAMPUS CENTER BLDG 86E

    Both now key as 100 CAMPUS CENTER with unit BLDG 86E, so the pair blocks and compares. BUILDING is still an ordinary street word where no identifier follows it (1 EMPIRE STATE BUILDING, 4 BUILDING COMMISSION RD).

    • A test asserts the general case over .np_street_types: every key whose abbreviation is a designator must be a designator itself. This class of bug is invisible one case at a time, because the street key looks right.
    • This moves the signature, to v1-6d90b52d8b781673. Any address spelling the designator out keys differently, so cached keys and the corpus statistics built on them must be rebuilt.

  • np_unit_id() is gated by the designator pattern, so it returns NA for a line that names no unit instead of reducing whatever it was given. It is exported, and a caller handing it a raw address line got confident nonsense with no signal: "PO BOX 1367" gave "BOX1367", "LAS VEGAS" gave "VEGAS", "114 HIGH ST" gave "114HIGHST". All three are now NA.

    • A bare identifier with no designator ("300") is now NA as well, because a digit string alone is as often a box number or a record counter as a door. Pass a dedicated unit column as np_extract_unit()’s unit argument, where a bare value is still accepted.
    • np_normalize() is unaffected: it calls the internal .np_unit_id() on an already-extracted street_unit, and street_unit_id does not change.

  • New exported np_extract_unit(), the single-vector entry point onto that gate: it reads the unit out of one free-text address line exactly as np_normalize() fills street_unit. A consumer parsing one line no longer has to normalize a one-column data frame to reach the gate.

npnormalize 0.1.1

  • New exported np_unit_id(). It reduces a suite as np_normalize() writes it in street_unit ("STE 300", "# 300", "STE D-2") to its identifier ("300", "300", "D2"), which is the street_unit_id column.
    • matchdb’s md_unit_id() needs a public function for this, because it can no longer find npmatch’s internal .np_unit_id() once npmatch imports this package (step 3 of dev/EXTRACTION.md).
    • Like the other four wrappers, it adds nothing of its own, so the signature is unchanged: np_normalize_signature() is still v1-3e7b9f9d59bbb19e.

npnormalize 0.1.0

  • First release. npmatch’s normalizer moved into its own package, every function name and body unchanged (dev/extract-from-npmatch.R, from npmatch@de52bb9):
    • the rule tables;
    • np_normalize(), np_name_core() and np_name_placeholder();
    • the corpus statistics (np_name_freq(), np_token_idf(), np_addr_freq(), np_stopwords());
    • the blocking tokenizer;
    • np_normalize_signature().
  • np_normalize_signature() is v1-3e7b9f9d59bbb19e, as it was in npmatch, and a test pins it.
  • New exported wrappers for the internals npmatch’s matching code calls: np_tokenize(), np_doc_freq(), np_addr_key() and np_state_abb(). They are not part of the signature.
